summary: The queue points to detect.c:show_map_spot because its rn2(7) is the first unmatched C draw, but the frozen JavaScript never reaches that helper: read.js:seffects() records note_unported("read.c seffect_magic_mapping") for the cursed scroll. C’s whole read.c:seffect_magic_mapping() branch sets temporary confusion, calls detect.c:do_mapping(), and passes Confusion into detect.c:show_map_spot(). Frozen JS also hardcodes false in do_mapping() and refuses cnf=true in show_map_spot(). Matching this case requires the read effect and dispatch plus the dependent confused map path.

source.branch: A sighted Rogue on an ordinary mappable level reads a cursed SCR_MAGIC_MAPPING scroll while not already confused. C sets gk.known, temporarily sets HConfusion to 1, runs do_mapping() so every map cell reaches show_map_spot(..., Confusion), restores HConfusion to 0, then reports that the details cannot be grasped. The complete source function also handles blessed scrolls, already-confused reads, spellbook effects, and nommap levels.
callers: C direct caller: read.c:seffects() (2194-2290), SCR_MAGIC_MAPPING/SPE_MAGIC_MAPPING arm at 2263-2266. The target path is cmd.c read command at 1816 -> read.c:doread() -> seffects() at 635 -> seffect_magic_mapping(). Frozen JS follows js/cmd.js:runReadCommand -> js/read.js:doread() -> js/read.js:seffects(); the cursed-scroll arm at read.js:3322-3329 records note_unported instead of calling the helper.

C spell caller: spell.c:spelleffects() sends SPE_MAGIC_MAPPING through seffects() at 1528-1530. Frozen JS spell.js:spelleffects() omits SPE_MAGIC_MAPPING from its scroll-duplicate cases and reaches UnsupportedSpellCastError, so the spellbook entry point also needs caller wiring when the whole helper is ported.

C map path: read.c:seffect_magic_mapping() calls detect.c:do_mapping() at 2147; do_mapping() calls show_map_spot() with Confusion at detect.c:1430. The target recording reaches this path by reading the wished cursed scroll (input suffix "rh ").
dependencies: detect.c:do_mapping() (1422-1444): C passes Confusion to every show_map_spot() call and chooses browse_map()/redisplay versus reconstrain based on hero_memory and unconstrain_map(). Frozen js/detect.js supports only the hero-memory branch and passes false at 1627; the cursed path requires the temporary confusion state to reach this loop.

detect.c:show_map_spot() (1372-1419): the existing JavaScript port handles ordinary unconfused mapping, but throws UnsupportedSearchError for cnf=true. C first evaluates if (cnf && rn2(7)) at 1379; on successful cells it updates seen terrain and displays mapped terrain/traps/objects, while confused mapping skips engraving and room-discovery updates.

read.c:seffects() (2194-2290): its pre-dispatch exercise(A_WIS, TRUE) is already ported in js/read.js; the mapping effect does not clear *sobjp, so seffects() returns the unconsumed-scroll result and doread() performs normal discovery/useup handling.

attrib.c:exercise() is called before the effect and by detect.c:do_mapping() after the map loop; both calls use Wisdom and must preserve their source-order RNG/state changes. Its JavaScript port is in js/attrib.js.

read.c:seffect_magic_mapping() nommap arms call potion.c:make_confused() and polyself.c:body_part(); the mapping display path uses detect.c:unconstrain_map/reconstrain_map and display.c map, trap, engraving, redraw, flush, and browse helpers.

Other direct C callers of show_map_spot() are detect.c:do_vicinity_map() at 1504 and zap.c:zap_over_floor() at 3731. do_vicinity_map() is reached from spell.c:spelleffects() at 1576 and allmain.c:moveloop_core() at 412. Other direct C callers of do_mapping() are wizcmds.c:wiz_map() at 192 and sit.c throne handling at 153; this assigned scroll recording does not cover those entry points.

nethack-c/upstream/src/read.c:2102-2153 is the whole effect: it distinguishes scroll/spellbook, blessed/cursed, existing confusion, and nommap; for cursed unconfused mapping it sets HConfusion temporarily, calls do_mapping(), restores it, and emits the final message. read.c:2194-2266 dispatches both SCR_MAGIC_MAPPING and SPE_MAGIC_MAPPING; doread() uses seffects() at 635-645 and cmd.c maps the read command to doread() at 1816.

nethack-c/upstream/src/detect.c:1372-1419 and 1422-1444 establish the downstream state/RNG contract: show_map_spot() conditionally consumes rn2(7), updates map state/display on non-skipped cells, and do_mapping() passes Confusion through the complete x/y loop before its Wisdom exercise. Frozen js/detect.js:1585-1617 rejects cnf=true; js/detect.js:1619-1631 hardcodes false and implements only the ordinary hero-memory arm.

Frozen examined JavaScript at 3212f9f07c3fdf3f00c5c204885f51834f0b6448: js/read.js:2306-2321 restricts seffect_magic_mapping() to an uncursed scroll on a mappable level; js/read.js:3322-3329 routes the cursed branch to note_unported. js/spell.js:1429-1441 also omits SPE_MAGIC_MAPPING from its seffects caller cases.

Source reachability for this assigned case is cmd.c read command -> read.c:doread() -> read.c:seffects() -> read.c:seffect_magic_mapping() -> detect.c:do_mapping() -> detect.c:show_map_spot(). The current recording diverges at step 43, so it is not yet matching runtime evidence for the effect; after the port, verify the full replay. This case covers the cursed-scroll path only, not spellbook casting, clairvoyance/vicinity mapping, wand probing, wizard mapping, or the throne mapping caller.
